issues.detail: The Hebrew 'מָחַץ רֹאשׁ עַל אֶרֶץ רַבָּה' means 'he crushes the head upon/over a wide land' (i.e., the head of the enemy on a vast battlefield), but the Vietnamese 'nghiền nát đầu của đất nước lớn' renders 'đầu của đất nước lớn' as 'the head of the great nation/country', changing the object from a person's head (crushed on the ground) to the head/leader of a nation. This alters the meaning: the Hebrew has the head (of the enemy) being crushed on the wide earth, not the head of a country.
